toolArgs.question: Across my emails, Teams chats, and meetings in the last 60 days, what has {{inputs.accountName}} said about: (a) their Azure consumption plans, (b) competitor cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, OCI), (c) AI / EDA / HPC workload roadmaps, (d) any procurement, budget, or quota friction. Include date, source channel, sender/attendees, and a 1-2 sentence summary for each item. Cite specifically.

toolArgs.query: {{inputs.accountName}} consumption OR ACR OR MACC OR Azure spend OR Azure growth

nodes.topic: TACTICAL CONSUMPTION SYNTHESIS for {{inputs.accountName}} (TPID {{inputs.tpid}}). You have 8 source streams in your prompt context. Do the work in this order across your 6 thoughts: (1) From acr-trend, characterize the last 12 months — monthly ACR, MoM delta, identify any decline / plateau / under-pace signal. State the QUANTIFIED gap if one exists; if not, declare 'no shortfall; pivot to gap-creation framing'. (2) From ai-quota, find any model+region where utilization is at or above 80% of allocated quota — that is throttled real demand and a quota-uplift play. (3) From attached-products + msx-pipeline, list every Azure SKU family the customer is already buying — these are the lowest-friction expansion vectors. (4) From workiq-signal, extract every workload reference, every competitor mention, every roadmap signal the customer has uttered in 60 days. (5) Enumerate 5-10 specific expansion candidates as a structured list. For each: workload name, SKU family, estimated $/month at full landing, technical lift required (low/medium/high), 30/60/90 day timing, and a 1-sentence rationale citing which source streams support it. Show the $/month math (units × unit price × utilization assumption). (6) Self-critique: which two candidates are the weakest and why. Return strict JSON.

STRATEGIC CONSUMPTION SYNTHESIS for {{inputs.accountName}} (TPID {{inputs.tpid}}). You have the same 8 source streams. Your job is the offer-shape work, not the math. (1) From workiq-signal + teams-prior-plays, articulate the customer-truth — what does {{inputs.accountName}} actually want right now in their own words. (2) From msx-pipeline + pipeline-aggregate, map the stakeholders: who at the customer holds the wallet, who blocks, who champions; who on Brett's deal team owns each relationship. (3) Without seeing the tactical candidate list yet, declare a strategic frame for this account — is this a workload-migration play, an AI-capacity-unlock play, a FinOps-modernization play, a competitive-displacement play, a renewal-anchored expansion play, or something else. Pick ONE frame; defend it from the source data. (4) Design the offer-shape — incentive structure (MACC depletion accelerator? AzAcc? consumption rebate? engineering sponsorship?), engagement vehicle (POC / sprint / Architecture Design Session / FastTrack), success metric (ACR delta in N days). (5) Name the 3 plays you would prioritize at the strategic frame level (workload categories, not specific SKUs — the tactical-synth quantifies the SKUs). (6) State the single highest-leverage forcing function in the next 30 days that this motion should land against. Return strict JSON.

nodes.prompt:
You are running the think-tank workflow to produce a CONSUMPTION MOTION PLAN for {{inputs.accountName}} (TPID {{inputs.tpid}}). This is NOT an EBR. It is Brett's internal artifact for the deal team. The audience is the AE + SE + GBB + STU on this account. The output must answer ONE question: 'where is the $X/month of Azure consumption we are not currently banking, and what is our 30/60/90 day motion to land it.'

The 5 senior-fellow streams map as follows: (1) policy = trend analysis from runtime_inputs.acr_gap_summary; (2) economic = quantified candidate list from runtime_inputs.candidates with all $/month math intact; (3) legal = stakeholder map + commercial vehicle from runtime_inputs.stakeholder_map + runtime_inputs.offer_shape; (4) implementation = the 30/60/90 timing and technical lift estimates per candidate; (5) comparative = customer-truth and forcing function from runtime_inputs.customer_truth and runtime_inputs.forcing_function.

Produce: (a) plan_markdown — a 3-page Consumption Motion Plan in Markdown with sections: Executive Summary (the $/month opportunity in one sentence), The Gap (quantified), The 3 Plays (top-3 from runtime_inputs.prioritized_plays, each with: workload, sizing math, $/month, lift, timing, customer-truth tie-in, stakeholder owner, offer construct), The Asks (POC / sprint / capacity / sponsorship), 30/60/90 Roadmap, Risks & Counter-arguments; (b) peer_review_notes — what the internal review caught that should be addressed before the deal team sees this.

Draft an internal email to the {{inputs.accountName}} deal team. Recipients are in input deal_team_emails. The subject must lead with the headline_dollar_amount and the framing 'Consumption Motion: {{inputs.accountName}}'. HTML body, <250 words, this structure: opening sentence states the headline opportunity in $/month and the timeline. Bullet list of the 3 plays from the plan: workload — $/month — timing. Closing sentence: 'I have proposed three Working Session slots for next week; reply with your preference or add to the calendar.' Sign Brett. Output strict JSON with subject (string), html_body (string), to_emails (array of strings) — copy the to_emails from input deal_team_emails verbatim.

Compose an Adaptive Card JSON payload for the {{inputs.accountName}} deal-team Teams chat. Card title: 'Consumption Motion — {{inputs.accountName}}'. Subtitle: headline_dollar_amount over the next {{inputs.target_timeline_days}} days. Body: 3 fact-set rows, one per play from the plan (workload, $/month, lift). Action button: 'Open the Plan' linked to runtime_inputs.plan_webUrl. Output strict JSON with card_json (object) and chat_lookup_query (string — the search query the next node uses to find the deal-team chatId, e.g. '{{inputs.accountName}} deal team').

Render runtime_inputs.plan_markdown to a PDF file at exactly this path: ~/maenifold/output/consumption-strike/{{inputs.accountName}}-consumption-motion-{{inputs.run_date}}.pdf. Use pandoc if available; fall back to markdown-pdf or a Chromium headless render. Also write the source markdown alongside as a .md sibling. Return strict JSON with pdf_path (string) and md_path (string) — both absolute filesystem paths.
